How did you get Petra to teach you this?
You can do this dance to any music.
A nostalgic dance to help one simply feel better.
It is my firm belief that you should not have done that.
A very special salute for very special Guardians.
Those in the know are in the know.
A dance for the most contest-loving of Guardians.
"These are mementos of past Awoken Paladins. I don't know how the Fallen learned of them, but a Taken attack targeted the mementos… and desecrated them."
"Our honored dead deserve better. Take their mementos into the Shattered Throne and hunt down the Taken responsible. Their blood will avenge the wrong that's been done and purify the tokens."
"As for the bow…" Petra gives you a small, almost wistful smile. "I will not ask what passed between Sjur Eido and you. Hunt well, my friend."
"The past refuses to rest peacefully here. The Taken know this as well as we do, and recent assaults targeted the very history of the Awoken."
"I won't let the Taken go unpunished. Come see me as soon as you can."
The work of the Queen's Wrath is never done and neither is that of the Guardians.
The purified Awoken mementos belong with Sjur Eido, the first Queen's Wrath. Go to her statue and present them as an offering.

Petra holds out a case full of strange mementos. Despite their small size, their antiquity is apparent—as is the Taken corruption clinging to them. Petra starts to speak, and you hear righteous anger behind her clipped words.
The bow thrums with whispers from the past. Distant and haunting, like a familar but half-forgotten melody. It is not an entirely comforting sound.
A brief message from Petra Venj, the Queen's Wrath, awaits you.
Realizing that a bad situation doesn't mean you can't have a good time.
Working together as a team to achieve victory.
Paying attention to the enemies and communicating what you see.
Take a short break, Oath Breaker.

Teaching the strategies that have worked for you.
Paying attention to each player's strengths and weaknesses and using them effectively.
Checking the modifiers and adjusting your play style or gear accordingly.
Vendors have new weekly bounties each week. They take a decent chunk of time to complete, but offer substantial rewards.
Bounties are a strong source of experience for gaining Rewards Pass ranks and Artifact levels. Bounties are available for purchase from many Tower vendors as well as your planetary contacts.
The Eververse Store features a daily rotating selection of items that can be purchased with Bright Dust instead of Silver.
Daily bounties refresh each and every day with a new selection of things to do. Try them out—they shouldn't take you long!
Commander Zavala, Lord Shaxx, and the Drifter offer shaders and emblems each Season, achievable through focused investment in their respective activities.
Commander Zavala, Lord Shaxx, and the Drifter offer themed cosmetic upgrades each Season, achievable through focused investment in their respective activites.
Once you reach the Power cap—and powerful rewards no longer give you higher Power—the only way to advance is through pinnacle rewards. You can find pinnacle challenges in the Director.
After you reach a certain Power level on your gear, most activities and items no longer grant you progress. A consistent way to advance is to complete weekly challenges that award powerful loot.
Weekly challenges show up with a special icon in the Director. They offer significant experience gains as well as powerful or pinnacle rewards.

Repeatable bounties are expensive, but offer players the ability to earn consistent experience and other rewards that focus on one activity. You can hold only five repeatable bounties from a given vendor at once.
Exotic quests are challenging pursuits that award unique and powerful weapons. Many Exotic quests can be started from vendors in the Tower, but others must be discovered in the world.
Fikrul returns, wielding an Echo with the power to twist living Eliksni to his own ends.
Step into the role of Slayer Baron, raise the banner of House Light, and wield the paracausal powers of Eido's tonics against them.
The Dreadnaught lives again and surges with Taken corruption threatening to spread throughout Sol.
You must find the resolve and ambition to repel the Taken.
Become a conduit of corrosive power—the bulwark against chaos—and break the Taken with your will.
In the aftermath of the Witness's death, explore novel paracausal mysteries.
Delve into the core of the living planet Nessus, and pursue a ruthless new threat with a familiar face.
Embark on a perilous journey into the heart of the Traveler, rally the Vanguard, and end the War of Light and Darkness.

lines.text: "According to those blueprints, the one thing the Fallen haven't worked out yet is how to stabilize the Stasis energy. So I whipped up a prototype of my own." He winks. "This should help you get the gun firing."
I've picked up a few Fallen weapons in my time. Pretty impressive what they can do with some spare parts and grit.

lines.speaker: The Drifter

lines.text: Looks like there are some cracks in the empire now that Eramis is out. We can use that.

lines.text: With your new Skiff codes in hand, you're nearly ready to go after the Stasis weapon. First, Drifter wants to meet with you to give you a critical weapon component.
You successfully acquired the Stasis weapon from the Fallen. Drifter wants to take a look at it.

The Drifter examines the blueprints you found. Turns out that the Fallen are using Praksis's armor tech to create a weapon capable of channeling Stasis energy. Eramis had plans to distribute this weaponry to Fallen all across the system, expanding the capabilities of her army.

Drifter likes the idea so much that he immediately cooks up a plan to steal the prototype from the Fallen. He thinks Spider's associates might be able to offer some insider information too. While he looks over the blueprints and calls in a favor, he asks you to go to Europa and gather more intel on the prototype.

Drifter contacts you to let you know Spider's sending an associate to meet with you. She has some tech that will disguise your ship to appear on radar as a Skiff, letting you sneak into a back area of the city. She's waiting for you in a Lost Sector.
Team up with the Drifter to steal a Stasis weapon made by the Fallen.
You're ready to go after the Stasis weapon prototype. You've got all the tools you need to break in. All that's left to do is get the gun.
The Drifter has asked you to gather Fallen weapons intel while he inspects the blueprints you found. That might lead to more information about the Stasis weapon prototype.
You found some briefs that indicate the Stasis weapon effort is being led by a high-ranking Fallen lieutenant. Taking the lieutenant down could gain you more information about the gun's whereabouts.

You discovered intel that suggests the Stasis weapon is being held in the Fallen city. Drifter's going to find you a way in. In the meantime, practicing with Stasis will be good preparation for learning to use this experimental gun.
Drifter is impressed. He admires the gun and asks you to bring it through Gambit sometime. This weapon could really shake things up.

Uh uh. Not quite yet. The blade is only for those who can handle its power. Sure, you've proven yourself somewhat. But I'll need to see you survive one of the training modules built for Exos first. Best of luck.
lines.speaker: Clovis AI

lines.text: Lookin' like some of those flashes are of me trudging through ice and snow, passin' bodies of my fellow Exos. One of 'em looked to be surrounded by Vex technology, another amongst the ruins of an old city, and another surrounded by factory equipment. The rest are a blur… Shame I left 'em behind. Wish I knew why. Bet you might figure that out.
lines.speaker: Banshee-44

lines.text: Not sure what exactly we're looking for in that bunker. But my instinct tells me it's some way to mend that Broken Blade. Look for a bunker hidden beneath the ice. That's the best I got for ya.
lines.speaker: Banshee-44

lines.text: Those Dead Exos you found are giving me a headache something fierce—and even more flashes. That blade again, in more glory than before. Must be important. Also saw frozen-over labs filled with dormant Exos. Even saw one the size of a giant. Gonna take a guess and say that's your next stop… wherever it is.
lines.speaker: Banshee-44

lines.text: Oh, did I forget to mention it was broken? Not my problem. Perhaps this Banshee friend of yours can help. Until next time.
lines.speaker: Clovis AI

lines.text: This isn't the first time the Vex have tried to destroy me and everything I've built. I hate to admit it, but I need your help, and I need it immediately.
lines.speaker: Clovis AI

lines.text: "This thing is givin' me flashes left and right. But they're scrambled. Something about a bunker hidden away among the ice. Must be Europa. Gotta ask you to help one more time. We're close, I can feel it."
"I've got questions, and it sounds like I've also got answers. Hopefully I've got nothing left to answer for."
"Bunch of Guardians storm the Deep Stone Crypt and next thing I know, I wake up in a daze sprawled out on the floor.
lines.speaker: Banshee-44

lines.text: "Seems crazy to assume the two are connected, but then again, stranger things and all that, y'know?
lines.speaker: Banshee-44

lines.text: "Now you walk in here and my insides go haywire all over again.
lines.speaker: Banshee-44

lines.text: "Lotta weird images flashin' through my mind. Hard to make sense of 'em all. Vex… a blade… And a few dead Exos on Europa, unhappy with their lot in life, I imagine.
lines.speaker: Banshee-44

lines.text: Not sure what that's about. Maybe see about findin' 'em? Help me make sense of all this. I'll be waitin'.
lines.speaker: Banshee-44

lines.text: Last thing. I swear. There's still a number of Vex running around. Some too dangerous to leave unattended. Escort them out of this life, and I'll give you what you're after.
lines.speaker: Clovis AI

lines.text: Well then, perhaps I owe you the other side of quid pro quo. The blade you're looking for was broken into pieces somewhere in the Glassway. By now, the Vex have likely found it themselves. Someone as capable as you should have no issue retrieving it from them. Now leave me be.
lines.speaker: Clovis AI

lines.text: Seems like we have a lot to discuss. The visions haven't stopped, but I think I get it now. You know where to find me.
lines.speaker: Banshee-44

lines.text: I know you desire the blade. But you can't have it just yet. I'll need a few tasks completed first. It's been a while since I've been… awake. And now this alien race you call "Fallen" infest MY colony. They must be dealt with in short order. See to it.
lines.speaker: Clovis AI

lines.text: You really want to help your friend, Banshee? Start by eliminating any Vex you can find. They've long been more than just a pain in my side. One day, they will answer to us. Until then, see that they're dealt with.
lines.speaker: Clovis AI

The stately and inscrutable ruler of the Reef.

It seems you've discovered my grandfather's Exo training protocols. They were designed to hastily upgrade the physical and mental fortitude of newly built Exos. But their design contained a rather 'dark' secret, as did most things built by my grandfather. Be careful within them; I imagine they won't play nice.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: "Old secrets emerge in the wake of your kind invading the Deep Stone Crypt. Something siphons power where it didn't before, in Bray Exoscience."
"Investigate, yes?"

Though Eramis dug deep, she did not uncover every secret buried within the ice. Long before our arrival, Europa thrived through scientific discovery during your Golden Age. "I've looked beyond this reality," said Eris Morn, lacing her hands together in front of her face. "Beyond Light and Darkness."
"I've seen Ahamkara, slain by my own blade. I've seen time broken, and the veil of causality sundered."
"I've seen my fireteam murdered, and their phantoms manifested to torment me." Eris stared off into the middle distance. "I've seen many things I wish I could forget."
"You've really seen it all," Glint said. "And blindfolded!"
"But what if—"
"Not even once, Little Light," Eris said with finality. "Not even on the Moon. I would have remembered."
"Cayde used to tell stories about the Headless Ones," Ikora recounted with a wry smile. "He said he killed dozens of them on the Moon. The way he told it, they exploded like piñatas."
"Just promise me one thing," she said. "If you do find something, tell me. Tell everyone. Cayde would've liked that."

"Well, Glint, I wouldn't classify that as evidence per se," Cryptarch Matsuo hedged. "The spontaneous creation of similar legends in disparate cultures is a well-documented phenomenon. Even in the absence of direct communication. Some scholars call it 'simultaneous invention.'"

"For instance," he continued, "the Yetis of Himalayan folklore and the Lumbering Jacks of North American legend. Both reclusive ape-like creatures said to populate the wilderness. Or the Centaur of Greek mythology and the Sheepdog of Northern Europe. Both mythical creatures said to be hybrids of other species. Etcetera."
"I have heard tales of such creatures," Mithrax said, his deep voice resonating through the ruins. "Those with eyes of flame. Tormented by endless burning."
"Some say they were once Hive, twisted by foul experiments." He paused to take a pull from his rebreather. "Others say they were Guardians who turned to Darkness."
"Has anyone from House Light seen them?"
"Yes?" the Ghost prompted. "What about him?"
"Yes, it is so," the enormous Kell nodded. "Klyfiks is an idiot."
"Bray used the tools of the Vex, while Hive blasphemers practiced the magical art of necromancy." Her tone darkened. "Both succeeded, after a fashion."
"The early Hive experiments were done in secret, under the guidance of a powerful Wizard, whose name we'll not mention here."

"Yes," Ylaia grimaced. "The unmentionable Wizard created many abominations, using deceased and living subjects, including your unfortunate Moon miners." She steepled her fingers. "It's possible that access to these powerful 'pumpkins' were a boon to his research."
"Wow, that explains a lot," Glint marveled. "But…" he continued reluctantly, "pumpkins aren't powerful relics. They're just… fruit."
"They are indeed," Ylaia concluded direly, "the fruit of the damned."
"You're not going to make fun of him, are you?" the administrator asked with a raise of her eyebrow. "He's been through enough already."
"Just the opposite," Glint assured her. "I'm one of the few people who actually believes him!"
"Robots who believe in the Headless Ones." She shook her head. "It boggles the mind."
"I think we're sentient energy signatures, housed in a cybernetic construct," Glint said, trying not to be offended. "But I do have an internal database, if that's what you mean."
"But if it's not a glitch, then… what the hell is it?"
"How could they chop off their own heads?" Saint-14 interjected. "It makes no sense. They would die halfway through."
"Well," Glint replied, "they could have built some kind of device. A guillotine, maybe?"
"I respect your commitment to this research," Geppetto said. "But unfortunately, there's no hard evidence supporting your claims."
"Bah," Saint-14 scoffed. "People say many things. You should hear what the Eliksni say about me…" He looked at the floor and scuffed his feet. "Not everything you hear is true."
"I'm happy that you're taking time to rest," Geppetto said, bobbing encouragingly. "After everything you and Brother Crow have been through, it's well deserved. Just… don't get your hopes up."
"Oops," the AI said. "I accidentally knocked the board over. How clumsy of me."
"Well…" Glint fidgeted, inching toward the exit. "I should get back to the Guardian. We're going to visit your neighbors!"
"But come again," the AI continued, "and I'll tell you everything you want to know about the Hive necromancer who ripped the concept of Headless Ones from the Human subconscious."
"…But only if I come back to visit, right?"
"That's right," said Failsafe, smugly. "I hear that's called 'incentive.'"

"Glint! It's good to see you," Eva exclaimed. "I've been enjoying your additions to our little collection." She patted the Book of the Forgotten. "Though, it makes me sad to think of all those poor lost souls, driven mad by this or that. Even if they are just tall tales."
"Actually," Glint chirped, "the Guardian and I are close to proving once and for all that the Headless Ones are real!"
"My goodness." Eva shook her head in disbelief. "Then again, I shouldn't be surprised. This system keeps getting stranger and stranger."
"Klyfiks will tell you what he has seen, but he must receive something in return." She bobbled her head slightly, which Glint interpreted as equivalent to an eye roll. "He wants his own Sparrow."

"Just so. Klyfiks claims," she emphasized the word and paused to make her skepticism clear, "that during one of these battles, he sheltered in some ruins near the crash site. Inside, he says he saw a being with a round, bulbous head and flames for eyes."
"Tomorrow, we begin our search for the machine tower. But still, there's a nagging suspicion: is this some kind of collective glitch? Is it all just in our heads?"

"Man, they can say whatever they want. I saw what I saw," the man affirmed. He motioned to the proprietor for another pitcher. "They always tell you: report everything. No detail too small. You never know what matters most."
"Buncha bullcrap," he grumbled. "I saw what I saw."
"It had a big, smiling pumpkin head!" he shouted belligerently. "With three eyes! And purple flames shooting out of it!"
"I SAW WHAT I SAW, DAMN IT!"
"…that way, when they lit the candle, it would light up the face carved into the pumpkin!"
"It was," Glint nodded. "Humans used to put this pumpkin head all over the place. They would even paint them on their—"
"The Headless Ones," Glint encouraged her. "I'm really trying to make that name stick. I think it's pretty neat."
"They've been hanging around in those ruins for centuries," Failsafe continued brightly, "but they've never once come to say hello."
"They probably don't want to be smashed by rampaging Guardians," the AI responded dourly. "How should I know?"
"Your disingenuous compliment has been noted and appreciated," Failsafe replied, the lilt returning to her voice. "Would you like to play checkers?"
"One hundred and forty-three minutes," Glint said. "It was quite impressive. Crow can barely sleep for an hour without yelling at invisible enemies."
"The invisible enemies are the most dangerous," Ylaia responded. "Just look at Savathûn."
"Speaking of invisible enemies," Glint segued, "I wanted to ask you about a sinister group of pumpkin-headed monsters called the Headless Ones. Maybe you heard of them during your training?"
"Thanks, Failsafe!" Glint scooted into the ship, away from the prying eyes of the Vex and Fallen. "I know the Vanguard hasn't been back here in a while but—"
"Correct! It's been almost two years since you last visited, even though you promised to come back often," the AI replied. "I've since developed the emotion of betrayal, just for you!"
"Well, I'm here now." Glint tried to keep his tone light. "I was hoping you could help me with a research project?"
"Of course. I'm happy to be exploited for your gain!" Failsafe replied helpfully. And then, in a more dour tone, "Anything to break up the unending loneliness."
"I'm hoping you could tell me about the Headless Ones." Glint uploaded all the information he had to Failsafe's mainframe. "I have intel that they're around here somewhere."
"You are correct," the AI replied. "They're my neighbors! And they're the absolute worst."
"It's my turn next."
"As you can see, pumpkins featured heavily in the iconography of the time. People would paint them all over their bodies. Even in highly inconvenient locations."

Mithrax emitted a series of low clicks, which Glint took as grumbling. "Klyfiks, our engineer, says he witnessed the creatures on Nessus. But…" The enormous Kell seemed to be struggling with a translation.

I'm reluctant to report that I had another sighting in the glacial cave near Cadmus Ridge. This time, I managed to get a good look at the creature with my rangefinder. The body was unmistakably that of a Hive Knight, while the helmet (or head?) appeared to be that of a… pumpkin.
The pumpkin appeared to have a face carved into it. Three eyes and a big smiling mouth. With… flames shooting out.

We're not the only ones surveying this crash site. Fallen have been pouring into the area, fighting with Vex for control of the wreckage.

For now, we've dug in to some subterranean ruins just west of the downed ship. We're covering the entrance and can hold our position so long as they don't find an access point to our flank, but there's just too many for the four of us. We'll need reinforcements if we want to secure the site.

Just then, a Guardian wearing a ferocious chicken mask offered Eva some candy. She politely declined.
They giggled like schoolchildren, and for a moment, all their worries were forgotten.
Had my first bout of predormital sleep paralysis last night. It was expected, given the insomnia. What I didn't expect was for it to feel so real. Now I understand why the miners are scared.
The figure standing over me was a shadow, but also solid. My mind was a hundred percent convinced it was physically present. Terrifying.
Another surprise was how familiar the shadow seemed. I had the eerie feeling that I would have recognized it, if I could have just seen its face.
Eido translated Glint's question to Klyfiks, who sprawled across his chair with an air of self-importance. The two conversed for almost a minute before Eido turned back to Glint.

Glint quickly scanned his internal database for decommissioned Sparrows and identified several old models that he thought would be to Klyfiks's liking. When Eido relayed Glint's optimism, the engineer's mandibles clicked in what the Ghost assumed was excitement.
Glint met the former Hidden agent in a sake bar called the Drunken Noodle. He had agreed to speak on the condition of anonymity and was already drunk when Glint arrived.
The bar fell silent. The man suddenly felt everyone staring.
There was a long pause as Ylaia studied the hologram Glint had projected for her.

The Tech Witch furrowed her brow, piecing together many fragments of disparate lore. "If these legendary 'pumpkins' were tools for seeing beyond the veil of death," she mused, "then it makes sense that they would become the emblem of…" She looked at Glint expectantly.
I also realized why I didn't recognize it sooner. it's because that version of me, from whatever time or dimension… he doesn't have a head.

Off the record: your last report has been making its way around the Tower. It's become… a bit of a joke. So, when they debrief you, just keep your mouth shut about this pumpkin nonsense. Play it off as exhaustion, an optical illusion, or whatever, and you'll be back in the field in no time.

"No, you're not, but I'm going to clear this place out and make sure nothing is amiss. Get on home, ok?" They nodded and turned away. He added, loud enough for them to hear, "And no more rituals. You don't know what could happen if you accidentally mix real spells together."

"I put this book together with all the things we found during our research," Rhea said. She gently placed the book on its stand at the altar. "My mentor…" Her voice faltered. "She always said to keep your notes in one place, so they're easier to find… She never liked things to be messy."

"I was going to join him. I was supposed to be there," Nirysk said. "But I was a coward. I turned back. He… he didn't look at me with shame, only understanding, and that somehow makes it worse. I should have given my life to protect the Great Machine, too."
"Stop fidgeting, Nirysk," the young Eliksni girl muttered, tightening her grip on the other Eliksni's hands. "You don't see Cash or Rhea fidgeting."
"If you're scared, I'm sure we can do this alone—"
"Well…" Melii started, then paused. She looked hesitantly at her peers. "We were talking about how many people fell during the war, and, uh, we just wanted to try to speak to them."
"We don't care about stupid pranks," Rhea explained quietly. "We had heard that this time of year was the best to try something like this…"

"Everything has been moved to a vault designated by Ikora, for future inspection," Glint reported. "She thinks one of those Hive swords might have been real, so she's sending someone to investigate the market where the kids got everything."
"You've been busy, and I didn't want to waste your time with what looked like a prank—"
"I'm never too busy for you, Glint," Crow said, sincerity in every word. Glint's shell slumped a little in response. "Were they alright, at least?"
"I think so?" Glint said. "As alright as one can be after everything… I think they just needed someone to talk to."

"Come here," Crow said and held up his hand for Glint to float to. He obliged and was taken by surprise when Crow pulled him to his chest for a tight hug. "I'm sorry I haven't checked in with you. I'll try to do better. I promise."

"You shouldn't think like that," Glint said, his tone soft and full of empathy. "I know that's easier said than done but trust me when I say, I understand. Someone I knew died, and I thought… 'Why not me?' It's so easy, isn't it? To blame ourselves and think we could have done something differently? 'If only I'd been there, maybe they'd still be here…'"
"How do you get past that?" Nirysk asked. "It just feels like… Ether draining out of me constantly and I don't know how to stop it."
"Time," Glint said simply. "You give it time… and you lean on each other. You get through it together."
"Wait," Melii said. Glint floated closer to them, and the Eliksni's eyes widened. "That's not just any Ghost, egghead! That's the Hunter Vanguard's Ghost!"

"I could ask you the same," Glint said. He looked at each of them in turn, but found his gaze drawn invariably back to the book. Even from a distance it didn't look special. "What in the world were you trying to do, exactly? Summon a Headless One?"
"What? No! That'd be ridiculous," Rhea said. "Everyone knows there's no way to do that."
"Yeah, exactly," Cash said. "We were trying to speak to the dead."
Ghost: Final Deaths are always a possibility. We all know that.
Ghost: I don't know why I came back.
Ghost: I… I don't know why it was me and not Targe. He was just as important as any of us.

Glint saw the teens running into an abandoned building and floated in behind them. The rays from the setting sun trickled through the windows, allowing Glint to find his way without providing his own light. Keeping to the shadows, he bobbed his way through piles of debris, passing half-finished murals on the walls until he found the room the pranksters had decided to make their hideout.

As he entered, he noticed a collection of curiosities that he couldn't quite place, but it was an unfamiliar book in one of the teens' hands that claimed his attention first. It looked thrown together; pages of varying quality and color poked out haphazardly, like an art project gone wrong.
Glint shook his shell from side to side.

Any other year, he'd have been excited at the idea of a potential ritual to summon a Headless One, but this year… This year, he simply wanted some time for quiet contemplation. Figuring out what had caused such a strange phenomenon could wait. It was a problem for him and Eido to revisit at a future date.
For his own peace of mind, Glint scanned the reliquary and was relieved to find that it was just packed full of candy.
Micah: I'm proud of you for expressing how you're feeling about this, Ghost. I know it can't be easy.
Micah: Targe's death was a tragedy. And so was yours.
Micah: No one could possibly have known you'd get a second chance.
Micah: And it's okay that you don't feel okay. Any one of us would likely feel the same.
Micah: You're not alone, Ghost. You are here and we're here for you… We'll get through it together. It'll just take a little bit of time.

Faint guitar music drifted through the streets of the Last City, barely audible over the buzz of citizens in the market. Glint's iris flicked between passing patrons and the pleasing festival decorations. His self-assigned patrol was barely a distraction from his racing thoughts, but it made him feel helpful to Crow and the Vanguard—even if they didn't know and were too preoccupied to care.
A nearby stand decorated with stained glass wind chimes caught his attention. He gave them a closer look, wondering how to get one back to Crow.
Eva: Welcome, little Lights. Thank you for joining us.
Micah: In the spirit of the season, and with recent events in mind, we wanted to hold this gathering to give you space to talk and share.
Eva: The Festival of the Lost is an opportunity to celebrate life and honor death. We often forget to do both and can feel much turmoil as a result.
Micah: Mihaylova is recording, but only so you can look back on your progress if you like. So please don't feel intimidated by her.
Nirysk and Melii looked at each other. One of Melii's arms wrapped around Nirysk.
Glint felt their sorrow deeply. They were all so young.
Nirysk kicked the pumpkin head just hard enough for it to tumble out of the circle they'd painted on the floor, its face dark and mocking.
Lexicon: Yes, the Witness is awful, but maybe we should try to move forward? It's dead. Holding onto anger will only poison us and our future.
Micah: That's an excellent perspective, Lexicon. Thank you.
Ghost: No, but… I think I will be.
Ophiuchus: Maybe it's inherent for all Ghosts to want to sacrifice themselves eventually. As morbid as that sounds.
Glint: I know… Should we just have a moment of quiet? For Targe?

No. No, no, no. According to all the research he and Eido had done on the Headless Ones over the years, this shouldn't have been possible. It shouldn't have been allowed to happen. Nothing in this room was real, or at least shouldn't have been able to power a ritual—the book! It had to have been the book.
The teens were lost in the trance of their spell, a palpable energy lifting them slowly from the ground.
This was only supposed to be a prank! Glint tried once more to reach out to the Vanguard, to Crow, but his radio was eating static. He did the next best thing.

There were some unusual objects in the room. Glint scanned them when he was sure no one was looking: colorful fabrics draped over various things, a hundred or so melting candles, counterfeit Gambit coins, swords that were supposed to be Hive in origin, candy dumped in a variety of buckets, boxes, and vases. Everything was a forgery, some sort of fake.

Two young Eliksni had been standing off to one side. At the Awoken girl's behest, they approached her in the center of the makeshift ritual circle. That was when Glint's eye caught something interesting. An altar, covered in more candles and smaller baubles that reflected against something familiar, an item he hadn't expected to find here: a golden reliquary container.
The teens stood in a circle. At the center was a pumpkin, positioned in the middle of an intricate symbol, painted with unsure brushstrokes, smudged to fix mistakes.
Confused, Glint tried again. Nothing happened. His sensors were jammed. He couldn't even send an SOS to the Vanguard.
A violet glow danced in his peripherals, demanding his attention. He spun around and, to his surprise, saw it was from the pumpkin head—eyes and mouth alight.
Glint noted the cautiousness in her voice. He floated higher to be level with their faces and saw how they all looked away from him, as if ashamed. Or… was it something more?

They'd lost people to the Witness, and they were looking for solace. For answers. They wanted to feel close to their loved ones again after having had them taken away so suddenly and without warning. Glint could understand that.
Ophiuchus: Targe was a pain, just like Zavala, sometimes… but he was a good Ghost.
Ophiuchus: You get used to someone's presence when you've been around them for so long. Even if you don't speak often.
Ophiuchus: I knew he was going to do it. Something reckless… But I thought he would make it out. He and Zavala have been in many a bind, so I foolishly thought this would be no different.
Ophiuchus: What was it like when you died?

A debate had started between the teens. While they were distracted, Glint could easily float unnoticed from one hiding spot to the next. They were arguing whether to use melted candy on their hands to bond them even further before the ritual, which resulted in huffs and objections. Cash sighed at the response to his suggestion.
He glanced over at the group for a moment. Having checked that their attention was elsewhere, he floated over to the altar for a closer inspection.
Glint: The war with the Witness was never going to end without losses. I don't think any of us wanted that, but we all knew that if it meant saving lives, we'd pay whatever price was asked.
Glint: But I've never felt a Ghost's death before.

Glint: I didn't know Targe for very long. The nature of our mission in the Pale Heart brought everyone's Ghosts together. I've talked with Ghost a lot in the past and consider us friends, but it was nice to be around Targe and Ophiuchus. To see things from a new perspective.
Glint: I wish I could have gotten to know him better.
Emotion welled up within the Ghost, and he struggled to contain it.
The teens were quiet. Glint knew it wasn't the answer they wanted. They were here in search of closure. Their hopes pinned on forged relics and fabricated rituals. All they wanted was closure.
Bee: We almost died during the War. I—I know that "almost" isn't as bad as "did", but… I haven't felt the same since then.
Micah: What you experienced is just as important. No need to minimize it.
Batt: We got grabbed. It looked like that was it, but then it disappeared.
Bee: We're alive because of you. Thank you.

Seems like we'll need more Darkness energy than usual to empower the key this time. So we'll take Stasis to some of our more powerful enemies. You've got this.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: Ana will come around… I hope. In the meantime, Clovis's journal has turned up another Stasis enhancement, and I want you to have it. You know where to find me.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: Digging further into Clovis's journal is really paying off. Or I should say, Clovis's Golden Age experiments with Stasis are finally paying off. At least they're doing so for us, and not for him. Come to me at the campsite and our findings are yours to keep.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: This is it. Communing with the Clovis AI should lead us to his final Stasis research… though I am hardly looking forward to speaking to him again.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: I don't just have a history with the man himself. The AI and I had troubles of our own long ago. In fact, it was I who shut him down in the first place. I doubt he'll be happy to see me again.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: The Skeleton Key requires further empowerment. Let's try something a bit more significant—somewhere you can take on many enemies with Stasis in a short period of time.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: Now that the Skeleton Key's empowered once again, bring it to me and let's untangle more of Clovis's secrets.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: The Skeleton Key's ready. Come find me at my family's secret bunker and use it to unlock the journal. It's time to expose that which Clovis desired to stay hidden.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: The Skeleton Key's nearly brimming with energy. One more boost should do the trick.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: This is a bit unusual, I know—but the Skeleton Key is not yet fully empowered, and we have an opportunity here to test our Stasis skills on ourselves. If you feel comfortable with that, of course. If not, continue to empower it through our enemies. It never hurts to thin their ranks.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: "If I never have to speak to that bastard again, it'll be too soon. At least we got what we came for. As usual, it's potent Stasis energy, but it needs to be harnessed. Come find me at the campsite and it's yours."

Poring through Clovis's journal revealed to me just where his next decryption algorithm is hidden, and how to empower the Skeleton Key to access it. The answer lies in the Vex, and as always, Darkness.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: With our journal decrypted, we know where the final bit of Stasis research is. Like I said, with the man himself. But before we reach the AI, the key will need to be empowered one last time. The journal implies the key should unlock something within the AI, and that we'll find what we're looking for in doing so. Start by using Stasis to empower the Skeleton Key with Darkness. We'll go from there.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: I know just the place to gain plenty of Darkness energy for the Skeleton Key: Gambit, or as I have sometimes referred to it to poke fun, Drifter's Darkness Revue. Using Stasis against our enemies there should give you the boost you need.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: You're very close. There's a Fallen Captain that's been holed up, causing trouble in one of the Exoscience buildings. Taking them out should do it.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: You've done it. Now hurry to me. I invited Ana along this time after our last conversation, and we have much to uncover together.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: One final burst of energy, and we'll have what we need to face the Clovis AI together. There's a Fallen Captain that's been making its way towards him. Taking it down should be all you need.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: I realize now, our search for the Stasis Clovis found will always intertwine with my family's past, and my dark future. I'm sorry I left abruptly… but talk of family… always makes me uncomfortable.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: Perhaps one day, Ana and I will be reunited. Until then… Clovis's journal may have led me to find something Stasis related. If so, I think you should have it. Come find me near the campsite in a bit.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: Let's cap it off with a bit of Ether. Another of House Salvation's 'elite' have taken residence over in the Exoscience building. Put an end to it.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: In Clovis's research, he discovered traces of Darkness energy in every one of his subjects. Humans, Vex, even animals. We know now Darkness truly does reside within us all. Further decrypting Clovis's journal has pinpointed our next decryption algorithm, but to get there, we must begin by empowering the Skeleton Key with Darkness.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: Clovis left behind a Skeleton Key to the secrets of Europa, but never told me how to use it. In my dark future, I figured out it needed to be empowered with different types of energy. I used it to unlock Clovis's journal then. But in this timeline, it remains locked.
lines.speaker: The Exo Stranger

lines.text: The Exo Stranger shares that you'll need an immense amount of Darkness energy to empower the Skeleton Key this time. She asks that you take on powerful combatants to do so.

lines.text: You can't win them all, but you can always make the enemy remember you.

lines.text: A well-placed grenade can turn the tide of a fight.

lines.text: Keep moving, and you'll have a fighting chance.

lines.text: We Guardians depend on our fireteams… but sometimes you'll have no choice but to stand alone.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Our immortality isn't absolute.

lines.text: No matter how many times you fall in battle, your goal must be to stand at the end.

lines.text: Zavala may carry the shield of a Sentinel today, but you should have seen what he could do as a Striker.

lines.text: What may be allowed to come to light inside the Void?

lines.text: You should be throwing grenades as I say this!

lines.text: Your Light may take many forms. Hone them all.

lines.text: Many battles have hinged not on the victors' skill, but their timing.

lines.text: There's beauty in watching so many Guardians wield their Light all at once.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: How many will fall before you do?
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Each Guardian you face only makes you stronger.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Momentum is a fleeting thing. You have it one moment, but it may be lost the next.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Show your opponents you mean business.

lines.text: Whether attacking or defending, every small victory counts.

lines.text: Entering the Crucible on an empty stomach isn't usually a good idea, but there are exceptions to every rule.

lines.text: You're going toe to toe with some of the best the City has to offer. Good luck.

lines.text: Territory control is one of the surest paths to victory.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Leave none standing.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: I know they're not flashy, but Ghaul reminded us that we abandon them at our own peril.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Use your Light well, and it will power others.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Every second you hold territory is a second closer to claiming victory.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Yes, you have to give them back at the end of the match. We still practice proper sportsmanship here.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: The heat of battle cannot be tempered through Stasis—if anything, this power has only stoked the flames.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Control the resources of the battlefield. Deny your opponents the chance to use them.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Your opponents won't let their crests go without a fight.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Let's kick it up a notch, shall we?
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: The Crucible is more than victory or defeat. It's a lesson.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: The Void comes in many flavors. Give them a taste!
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Every successful offensive starts with a foothold.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: A skilled Guardian calling upon their Light is the most beautiful—and terrifying—thing you'll ever see.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Skirmishes between Guardians weren't always so… organized. My Crucible focused that energy into bringing us together rather than tearing us apart.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: I'll tell you the tale of a general, who sliced through an impossible knot…
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: When your sight fails you, listen, feel, or just run away!
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Between the two of you, nothing can stand in your way.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Stars don't twinkle. They burn with an impossible fury.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: The strength of a fireteam is greater than the sum of its Guardians.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Nothing like a little shock to get you moving in the morning!
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Sometimes you just have to take matters into your own hands.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Every round is a fresh opportunity for victory.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: It's important to maintain a balanced arsenal. You never know what foe you may face.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

"But after he stopped, the creature was not felled. Instead," she said, her voice dropping to a low rasp, "it advanced."
"Purple flames poured from the creature's eyes," she said, leaning forward. "It let loose a deafening shriek—"
"And when the scream ended, Phyzann of House Dusk, the Drowned Captain, had disappeared," Eido whispered, "…and was never seen again."
"Would you like… some tea?"
"Yes," Eido answered. "I do not believe they are of Hive origin."
"He tripped and fell on his own damn sword," Drifter corrected. "A little different."
"But it didn't kill him?"
"Nah, he left that to the Guardian."
"But the ode claims—"
'If I knew we would fight, I'd be long gone.'"
"I have ample evidence for their existence. I know that they have flaming pumpkin heads, and that they're filled with candy," Eido said stiffly. "And loot. They are also filled with loot."
"You heard about this from Glint?"
"So, if the Headless Ones were created by Nokris as you claim," Eido concluded, "how could they come to populate a cavern on Earth?"
"Maybe some Headless Ones hitched a ride from the Moon," Glint posited. "Like stowaways of cosmic evil!"
"Perhaps," Eido replied, unconvinced. "Or perhaps they are not of Hive origin after all. We may not have enough data yet to draw any conclusions."
"But one thing we can clarify right now," she continued, "is why the Headless Ones are so poorly named. Obviously, they have heads."
"I believe you're due for congratulations," Eido continued, "and several apologies. Your work revealing the Headless Ones was a feat of rare scholarship."
"Well thank you for saying so," Glint chirped. He seemed to double in size as his shell swelled with pride. "When I started my investigation, everyone laughed at me, but who's laughing now?"
"I… I'm not sure," Eido admitted. "Is it Drifter? He sometimes snickers at my expense."
"No," Glint explained patiently. "It's me. I'm the one who's laughing."
"Oh!" Eido exclaimed. "You're laughing as an expression of vindication! I understand."
"Fascinating," Eido agreed. "However, I do have a few questions about your conclusions…"
"If pre-Golden Age Humans knew of the Headless Ones," Eido said, "then they cannot be of Hive origin."
"A reasonable deduction," Cryptarch Matsuo affirmed. "Humanity's first contact with the Hive didn't occur until sometime during the Collapse."

"I suspect so," Matsuo replied. "Speaking of Glint… if you could omit my contribution to your research, I would appreciate it." He tapped his forefingers together carefully. "I was rather dismissive of Glint's early expeditions, and I have no desire to eat crow now."
"None of us desire that," Eido chittered, aghast. "I suspect he would taste… bitter."
"And these 'Headless Ones,'" Caiatl began, tilting down her tusks in contemplation, "they are warriors?"

"Oh yes," Eido said, looking up at the Cabal empress. "In fact, they may be Cabal in origin. I am investigating the stories now. Your retainers mentioned a similar tale, and I understand your people have a strong oral tradition. Surely there are accounts of flaming heads? Swords of unusual size?"
"There have been Cabal who have eaten fire, walked through fire, and belched fire. But that is all."
"There WERE many warriors with their heads on fire," she offered in consolation. "But not continuously."
"The odes say he was a ferocious warrior," Eido prompted, "who killed many Cabal. They speak of his bravery."
"Phyzann was incompetent," Mithrax grumbled. "He once blew a hole in the side of his own Ketch attempting the Rite of Six Hands with a live grenade. He was a buffoon."
"Yet the odes—"
"Odes are for hatchlings!" Mithrax replied, more forcefully than intended. "They make glory of desperation, and bravery of ignorance."
"As a Scribe," he continued more calmly, "you must learn to see the truth in such wishful thoughts."
"Yes," Glint said. "They stopped at the side of the road, because the Sparrow broke down. One went to look for supplies, and the other waited inside and locked the doors."
"The Sparrow had doors?"
"This one did," Glint said. "And they were locked. But then the Guardian heard a scratching at the door! From outside!"
"And a voice said, 'Let me in!' and the Guardian opened the door, but… there was nobody there!"
"I've conducted an interview with Empress Caiatl already. But I am hoping that you could further illuminate the subject."
"I am searching for information about the Headless Ones, and—"
"I'm so sorry, I—"
"I didn't mean to—"
"To upset you."
"As you can see," Matsuo continued with a self-satisfied smirk, "this report was written by a Golden Age scholar who describes himself a 'fourth grade' researcher."
"He calls this document a 'book report,'" Eido noticed. "There must have been a larger body of inquiry into the subject than we ever imagined!"
"Absolutely," Matsuo affirmed. "And this report identifies the individual who I believe discovered the very first Headless One…"
"After the Drowned Captain disappeared," Eido said to the gathered hatchlings, "the Cabal claimed the cavern as their own."
"But the very first night of their occupation, a figure appeared in the mouth of the cave," Eido said. "It had a big round head, and flames poured from its giant mouth. It was… a Headless One!"
"During that time, children would run amok," Cryptarch Matsuo explained. "They would extort foodstuffs from the citizenry under threat of vandalism."
"…When docile hatchlings acted as bandits," Eido supplied, "and the dead returned to speak with the living."
"Exactly," the Cryptarch nodded. "And those without heads were granted replacements… for a time."
"Yes. I hypothesize that they were created as part of an ancient Human ritual," Eido replied, oblivious to the Ghost's indignation. "…called the Hall Between."
"The realms of the living and dead," Eido reasoned. "To which the ancient 'pumpkins' were key."
"So, while I appreciate your discovery of the Headless Ones," Eido continued, "I cannot support your conclusions regarding their origins."
"I must reiterate that they do, in fact, have heads," Eido insisted in exasperation. "It's their defining feature."
"Spider, I wish to ask you about Phyzann, the Drowned Captain," Eido prompted. "No doubt you've heard the odes."
"There was a reason Phyzann died guarding a hole in the ground," Spider chortled. "Craask knew he was a liability."
Who saw a final dishonor at the hands of an enemy.
Many times this story has been told: we tell it again.
Few could stand their might, so great was it.
They took what was there to be taken, lives and loss.
Heads aflame, their end was found in endlessness.
No more wandering or warring in these lands.
Eido loomed over the gathered hatchlings, who huddled together nervously. Drifter loitered nearby.
Drifter, sensing his cue, let loose a blood-curdling scream, causing the hatchlings to jump and chitter in fright.
Whether these gourds were killed, cooked, and eaten is a… point of debate. Perhaps after a time, they were angered at being hunted for food and eventually turned on their predators.

The trip to Luna had been a short one, but now Eido sat uncomfortably in a folding chair in Eris Morn's dwelling. Her host poured steaming liquid from a vessel into a small ceramic cup. The Scribe took it politely, trying to keep the contents from spilling over the rim.

The Scribe looked down at her tea. Humans tended to drink such things communally, but Eris had not poured a cup for herself. Letting her eyes wander, Eido realized the room was oddly bare but for the teapot and a tattered mat at the door's threshold. The lettering on it was illegible.
Phyzann of House Dusk, loyal to Craask, Kell of Kings, slayer of Lightbearers and Cabal, lay silently beneath the dark waters.
The dull eyes of Cabal Legionaries peered thoughtlessly into the darkness, as they slogged through the water like livestock.

And when Phyzann rose up, blades gleaming in all four hands, roaring with the might of House Dusk, the Cabal cried out in their cruel and blundering tongue, their mouths fetid with fear, and they were slain.
From that day on, Phyzann of House Dusk had earned a new accolade among the Eliksni. He was henceforth known as the Drowned Captain.
Who took on a team of three Light-spawn.
Lord Saladin considered this. Eido could not discern what he might be thinking.
Glint's digital iris narrowed. He vibrated in a low whir, which Eido misinterpreted as thoughtful consideration.
Phyzann of House Dusk, loyal to Craask, Kell of Kings, was tested by wave after wave of Cabal intruders.

But each platoon that lumbered witlessly into his lair fell to pieces beneath the Eliksni hero's blades. Their entrails disgorged into the stagnant water, and their bleats of fear echoed off the cavern walls.
However, just as his victory was assured, the Eliksni hero felt a blade slide into his back, between his lower arms. A Dreg's knife, sharpened by betrayal, became his undoing.
And so Phyzann of House Dusk slid beneath the water once more.

It appears that most Humans used this license to contact their ancestors, similar to the Vanguard's severance rituals aboard the Leviathan. However, it is entirely possible that more adventurous practitioners used the power of the pumpkins to create entirely new beings: the Headless Ones.
During the rite, common Humans wore monstrous masks for cosmetic and spiritual purposes—a custom that survives via the Festival of the Lost.
Masked Humans were allowed, if not encouraged, to participate in banditry and extortion of their neighbors. This seemed especially prevalent among juveniles.
Mithrax fidgeted silently with the regulator on his Ether rebreather.
Eido wrung both sets of hands uncomfortably. The laboratory walls were lined with hundreds of canopic jars, filled with preserved organs and appendages. She recognized many of them as Eliksni.
Eido felt a soft, blooming sensation in the forefront of her mind. Gracious acquiescence.

The thought of a creature without a head sent up a spike of adrenaline, a flash of sickening terror that burst in Eido's mind so violently that she jumped. The Psion's own thoughts only compounded its fear. Eido's eyes widened.
Phyzann of House Dusk, loyal to Craask, Kell of Kings, lay betrayed. As his life-Ether flowed into the murky water, he heard a call.
It was not the call of his Kell, nor of his Dregs. It was not the call of the Great Machine, nor that of the Awoken prince.
It was the call of the Voice in the Darkness, which bade him to rise, reborn and remade in a form both terrible and terrifying.
And as Phyzann rose, no longer of House Dusk, he roared with flame that poured from his mouth and eyes, and his spirit longed for Ether no more.
The hatchlings muttered darkly, mimicking their elders' prejudices against the Cabal.
They fought with honor until honor fled them.
They found an enemy too fierce for them to fell.
To take to great caves and hidden places.
A final stand made to hoard their honor.

"I've sent a message to Ana. I can only hope she receives it well. Assuming she has any desire to speak to me, we will hopefully be seeing her soon."
"In more hopeful news, decrypting Clovis's journal has yielded another opportunity to enhance your Stasis powers. I can't wait to see what you do with it."
"My friend, you have no idea how grateful I am for you and all that we have done together. This is only just the beginning."
"This should help provide us even more clarity. And you, even more Stasis power. Once you're through attuning to it, return to me. I feel as though I owe you a million more thank yous."

"This journal of Clovis's is more of a boon for us than I previously realized. In my original timeline, there was a hard copy, though it was incomplete. You've finally helped me access its digital form, and with it, we've been rewarded."
"Our first step in enhancing your Darkness abilities begins with this. I'm looking forward to seeing what you make of it."
"The results would be disastrous."
"Perhaps I shouldn't have dropped so much on Ana at once. In my past attempts to befriend her—across other timelines—I always tried to ease her in to these revelations."

"But we no longer have time for ease. I just hope that by creating a different world—one where the Darkness can't get its filthy claws into our heads—that Ana will come around. If she doesn't… then this whole thing may be a wash once again."

"No, it can't be. This time, things truly are different. You're walking proof of that: you and your resilience to the manipulations of Darkness. So let's keep up the good fight by continuing to use Clovis's research for good. Speaking of, here's what I found this time. It's yours to do with as you please."

The Exo Stranger has poured over Clovis's digital journal and discovered that despite learning more about Stasis from the available pages, much of it is still encrypted. Turns out, Clovis didn't trust many, including his family.

Though this is not the Exo Stranger's first time seeing it, she has never been able to fully decrypt it to further understand its secrets. But with you at her side, decrypting the journal finally feels like a reality.

In order to decrypt and explore it further, the Exo Stranger once again asks you to empower the Skeleton Key with Stasis energy, believing that Clovis installed it in her hoping she would use it to one day continue his work and further his legacy.
You've just informed the Exo Stranger of your findings on Banshee-44. She's taken aback. This is news she hoped to take to her grave.

"According to Eramis, one of her people, an apothecary named Ixis, has been captured by Fikrul. Ixis has found a way to send messages on public frequencies from somewhere inside the Revenant Fortress. Fikrul either can't intercept her messages or doesn't care she's transmitting. I've studied notes from her that Eramis has passed on, but nothing beats firsthand experience."
"Fikrul remains immortal, but if you can find Ixis in his fortress, she may be able to help us concoct a tonic to defeat him. Or help my father."
"Guardian. This will be the best and final test of all that we have learned together."
"This tonic will alter the Ether that flows through Fikrul's body, filling him with Light. While the potion runs its course, he will be Eliksni, not Scorn."
"My hope is that Fikrul will be cut off from his Dark Ether just long enough for you to put an end to him. To bring him a final death, as the Ghosts say."
"I've had an injector prepared and delivered to you. I wish we could test it first—but we have to take advantage of Fikrul's arrogance while we can."
"I know you can do this, Slayer Baron. Our House trusts in you."
"I really can't thank you enough for your help with Eramis. We're on the same side of this fight. So long as her people are safe, it's in her best interest to help us."

"Just in time too. Scouts from the House of Light found something out in the Reef—a formation of asteroids, lashed together. Between the reckless approach to construction and their taste in architecture, it's safe to say the Scorn are involved. We're closing in on Fikrul's base of operations, and everyone's pitching in on a plan."
"But before you go—I have something for you."

"I've spent countless hours studying Nezarec's curse. I've come to believe it shares a few elements with Dark Ether. I haven't yet found a safe treatment, but I did think of a way to weaponize my experiments against the Scorn."
"I hope it can be of use to you in the field."

"Now that you've helped me establish direct contact with Ixis, I've had unfettered access to her tonic experience. And I think we've made a breakthrough. I've left you something at the holoprojector, along with instructions for its use."
"I'm the Scribe of our House. Even so, I don't know if I can find the right words to thank you for everything you've done."

"My father's soul is intact. The Houses of Light and Salvation are safe. You made all this possible. I really should thank you formally, as a Slayer Baron of our House. But I hope you know that I consider you a true friend."

"I don't know if we can call Eramis a friend, but… I owe her much. She could have taken the Echo and abandoned us, but she chose to help. Do you think our talks over the past few weeks got through to her? I'd like to think so."

"Maybe Variks really will rebuild the House of Judgment. Maybe we'll divide into many Houses once again. Maybe the Eliksni will drift away from Sol and find new worlds. For now… my people have a new Kell to unite them. To lead them along a path very different from the one that the Kells of old envisioned for us."
"You'll always have a place in that future, Guardian. And a place in the House of Light."
"Machine-spawn. This is Eramis, of no House, Echo-Bearer and Voice of Riis."
"I reach you from the outer edges of Sol, where I am departing this war-torn slum forever. That I leave my people under your blithe tyranny shall be another of my unavoidable regrets."
"The Echo believes I am still worthy. I've made so many compromises…. Can I truly say I am of old Riis?"

"Eido would have me stay, of course, using my new power to reclaim Scorn from the Darkness. But the Echo calls me home. Its song resonates through every drop of my being. It sounds like… gusts of Ether flowing through canyons. Roiling as clouds and condensing as dew."
"I shall build a new life with my family… and think of you no more."
"I greet you in the Light once again, Guardian. You have prevented another Whirlwind, and brought honor to the title of Slayer Baron."

"I am now Kell of Kells, but I do not embrace it with four arms. Though I feel the Light flow through me once more, I fear the God of Pain will always be with me. A lingering note of discord in my blood."
"I thought to make Eramis or Variks Kell of Kells, but they refused. Eramis offered me the Echo, but I could not accept. It has chosen her."
"Eido would keep the Echo in Sol, to clarify the Ether of the Scorn… but it is too great a threat. We cannot risk another mass corruption."
"Instead, Eramis will take the Echo far from this system. Perhaps she can finally create a new Eliksni homeworld, as she always dreamed."
"Besides, House Light has all it needs here: kin, allies, and the Great Machine above."

lines.text: Retrace your steps through the Throne World to glean new insights from old cases.
One of the files seems much denser than the others. A closer look reveals it's an abstract on Deepsight, written by Eris Morn.

Savathûn's Altar is one example of Deepsight's potency in this regard. The wounds spanning the desert suggest the Witness engaged in a similar process with Mars; retreading old ground to forge new paths in the future.
Of course, as Ikora is quick to note, this is a logic well-known to Guardians already, thanks to the guided battle-meditations she put into practice after the Red War.
You look up from the file. If Deepsight can help you glean new clues from old cases, it would be worth it to put Eris's theory to the test.
Discover new Insights by retracing your steps in weekly missions.
By retracing your steps through the Throne World, you've picked up enough clues to form a theory about Immaru's motives, if not his entire plan.
Interlopers. Not just Guardians, but any who trespass into the Throne World are the threat.
And the defense against them lies in the Dark-tinged Osmic Fragments and the runes imbued with Hive magic.
Just when you thought you had seen enough contradictions-in-terms in this investigation, up pops a Hive Ghost using tools of Darkness to protect a realm filled with Light.
In the meantime, there are other angles of the investigation to consider. Check the other Hidden reports for more leads.
By retracing the steps of old cases in the Throne World, you've gleaned new insights that push forward your current investigation.

"You didn't think I'd give Crow something and not cook up something for you too, right? Come onnnn," he says. "He got a shiny new cloak and, potentially, crushing responsibility. It's only fair that you get a new gun courtesy of yours truly."

"Now, I've gotta go figure out how to get the rest of this Screeb juice out of my clothes before the big battle." Cayde sniffs his cloak, still rancid from the Screeb slime, and recoils. He whispers, "…At this point, I might just burn 'em."
Cayde has something to give you. Go chat with him.

Cayde hears your approach and turns to you. He's holding a sniper rifle. While familiar in shape, its design certainly feels like Cayde has had his hands on it. He offers it to you.
Cayde crosses his arms and considers you for a moment. It feels as though the quiet is intentional, appreciating your presence, until he nods his head and pulls himself back to reality.
You, Cayde, and Crow set out to investigate an unknown threat that is stirring in the Pale Heart. Track it down and destroy it.

"Guardian," Micah says when the feed opens again. "I can tell already something has changed for the better. I'm processing the readings now. Give me a moment, but early prognosis is very, very hopeful."

"No harm, no foul," Micah says, though she'd clearly prefer the idea works. The slow process of eliminating what doesn't work isn't ideal for situations like these. "Sending you one of the locations I've dug up now."
The Witness's forces are still running wild in the Pale Heart. Before you can get into the place Micah mentioned, you'll need to restore balance to the larger area it's part of.
Although the specific workings of Light may be unclear, the injured Ghost is looking much livelier. Something has changed for the better.
You can sense some new strength from the Traveler rising in response to your actions. The Arbor may have something new to show for your efforts. Perhaps you should return there.

There's still more to be done. Micah mentions Ulan-Tan, a historical Warlock with theories about Light and Darkness which were considered dangerous at the time. All Light was part of itself, he had concluded: Ghosts connected to Guardians connected to the Traveler, inextricably tied together. Micah thinks—maybe—that the problem with this damaged Ghost is that they've been disconnected from the Traveler in some way and forced to rely only on their own Light.

She's found some places, deep in the Pale Heart, that she thinks are as close to the Traveler's unfiltered essence as you can possibly get. Maybe there you can join this Ghost's Light with the Traveler's again. And even if that doesn't help, you'll still know more than you did before.

lines.text: The Hidden have a list of Throne World weapons that can shed light on the link between Weapon Patterns and Osmic Fragments. Use that as a guide.

In other words, the Darkness energy infused in the Osmic Fragments from Fynch is compatible with the Relic. Those energy readings are strikingly similar to the Weapon Patterns used to operate the Relic. The Hidden think the fragments are essentially weak, incomplete Weapon Patterns, but they need more data to be certain.
Shape more weapons using the Relic to confirm this connection. By analyzing complete Patterns, you might be able to determine whether the Osmic Fragments are truly compatible with the Relic.

You confirmed that the Relic, when paired with Weapon Patterns, allows the user to reach through time, rearranging memories into weaponry. There's no telling what else it can do in the hands of a powerful entity like the Witness.

Ikora posited before that the Relic caused the temporal wounds on Mars's surface. You believe she's right, and that the Witness used the device to learn about the planet's Golden Age and Collapse, leaving Mars irreversibly damaged.

Your report states that the Weapon Patterns you used are essentially Darkness-infused "memory road maps" to the weapons the Relic creates. The Osmic Fragments are a weaker, incomplete road map—but with enough fragments, someone could build the equivalent of a Weapon Pattern.

The Relic is clearly capable of anything from creating weapons to tearing the fabric of reality. If Immaru gathers enough Osmic Fragments and finds a way to approximate the functions of the Relic—perhaps by using the runes you discovered in the Throne World—there's no telling what he might create.
In the meantime, there are other angles of investigation to consider. Check the other Hidden reports for more leads.
It's confirmed: the Osmic Fragments are similar to the Weapon Patterns, but much weaker. It would take many Fragments to add up to one Pattern.

Did the Scorn's temporary possession have an effect? Or is the resonance amplified by the nearby presence of the other fragments?

More importantly, do the Scorn know what Immaru intends to do with the Osmic Fragments? They must. If they know the runes are for some kind of Lucent Brood defense, then the Osmic Fragments are undeniably part of that.
It would help if you knew the runes' specific purpose. You glance at the Hidden's open query. No progress yet.
